# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen`. Edit the config schema or secret metadata instead. -->

`config.yaml` is validated by the [JSON Schema](../packages/contracts/config.schema.json). Paths below use `[]` for array entries. Required means required in that object; defaults may fill optional fields.

The JSON Schema cannot express every cross-field rule. Run `board doctor --offline` after editing the file.

In a listed repo, a PR whose check list on head is empty passes the Dev gate check condition instead of waiting in Dev. A list of only skipped checks still waits, and red or pending checks still count. A listed repo whose branch protection requires checks that have not reported yet also passes, so list only repos that run no checks. Without this key, a PR with no checks waits in Dev.                                                                                                                                                                |

| `projects[].link`                              | object  | no       | `{}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | —                                                                                                  | How a project links a PR to its task. A github-issues project reads an issue number from PRs in tracker.repo; a Jira project reads an issue key with one of tracker.projectKeys from PRs in repos. Left at the defaults, a Jira project links every tracker.projectKeys key (such as PROJ-12, any letter case) in the PR title or head branch. Set the sources and patterns to the branch and PR title naming rules of the repos. The board does not enforce those rules; the repo enforces them through its CI title check and its agents' skills. board doctor compares these rules with recent PRs by operatorGithubLogin. |
| `projects[].link.sources`                      | array   | no       | `["closing","branch","title"]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | min items 1                                                                                        | Where a PR names its task, in priority order; the first source that yields an issue number wins (for a Jira project, an issue key). closing: issues in tracker.repo the PR closes (Closes #12 in the body, or linked in the sidebar), for PRs to the default branch only; a Jira project skips it. branch: branchPattern on the head branch. title: titlePattern on the PR title.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `projects[].link.sources[]`                    | string  | no       | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | one of closing, branch, title                                                                      | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `projects[].link.branchPattern`                | string  | no       | `"^[A-Za-z]+-([1-9][0-9]*)"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | min length 1                                                                                       | Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR head branch, such as <agent>-<number>-<slug>. Branches longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR head branch.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `projects[].link.titlePattern`                 | string  | no       | `"^[a-z]+(?:\\([^)]*\\))?!?: #([1-9][0-9]*)"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | min length 1                                                                                       | Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR title, such as fix(core): #12 summary. Titles longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR title.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Session links

The Board links a Spur session to a task by three rules, tried in this order on every Spur poll. The first rule that names a task wins, except that a pull request match off the PR's head branch waits for the branch rule.

1. Explicit label. The session's Spur link `board-worker` is read first, then `board-other`; the first whose URL parses names the task. `board-worker` links the session as worker, `board-other` as other. The URL is `<Jira base>/browse/KEY-12` for a Jira task or `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/12` for a GitHub Issues task, with owner and repo spelled letter for letter as in `tracker.repo`, and with no trailing slash, query or fragment. A label that parses but names a task the Board does not track links nothing and turns off the next two rules for that session.
2. Pull request. The session's `pr` link is a PR linked to the task, and the session's Spur project is listed in that project's `spurProjects` with `role: worker`. When the session's branch equals that PR's head branch, this rule names the task. When it differs, or the Board has no head branch for the PR yet, the branch rule runs first; only if it names no task does the session link to the PR's task, always as other.
3. Branch. The session's Spur project is listed with `role: worker`, and its branch contains the task key in any letter case, not after a letter or digit and not before a digit (`WEBDEV-56` is not found in `XWEBDEV-56` or `WEBDEV-5698`), or equals the head branch of a PR linked to the task. Exactly one task must match. Sessions that share a branch in one poll stay unlinked unless the task already has a worker.

Scope: a `board-worker` or `board-other` label links a session from any Spur project. The pull request and branch rules need the session's Spur project listed in that project's `spurProjects` with `role: worker`. A worker still needs its Spur project in `spurProjects`, with any role, to call `board task`, `board ask` and `board comment`.

Roles: a session links to a task once, and that link keeps its first role. A session linked by the branch rule, or by the pull request rule on the PR's head branch, becomes worker when the task has no worker, otherwise other. A session linked by the pull request rule off the PR's head branch is always other. After `board unlink` removes a session, no automatic rule links it to that task again; `board link` restores it with its original role.

For a GitHub Issues task, a PR in `tracker.repo` links to its issue through `link.sources`, and PR discovery keeps only PRs whose author is `operatorGithubLogin`. Until that PR is linked, a session with an ordinary branch name links only through an explicit label.

Setting the label: `spur spawn` cannot set links. Set it on the new session with `spur slots --session <id> --link board-worker=<url>`; inside the session, `$SPUR_SESSION` holds its ID. Build the URL from the task key: `o/r#12` is `https://github.com/o/r/issues/12`.

Operator fallback: `board link <task> --session <session> --reason <value> --key <key>` links the session as worker when the task has none, otherwise as other.

Reviewers: a session of a `role: worker` Spur project whose `pr` link is a PR it only reviews, on a branch other than the PR's head, links to that PR's task by the pull request rule as other, even when the task has no worker. A review session checked out on the PR's head branch links as worker when the task has none, unless it sets `board-other` to the task's URL before its `pr` link appears. A later label changes nothing, because a link keeps its first role; the operator then removes the link with `board unlink <task> --session <session> --reason <value> --key <key>`. No automatic rule links it to that task again; `board link` restores it with its original role.

## secrets.env keys

Keep `secrets.env` private with mode `0600`. It lives beside `config.yaml` in the Board config directory, or under `BOARD_HOME` when set. Never put secret values in `config.yaml` or logs.

| Key                      | Required when | Purpose                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`           | always        | Read GitHub repositories and check runs.                                                |
| `JIRA_EMAIL`             | jira          | Jira account email.                                                                     |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN`         | jira          | Jira API token.                                                                         |
| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`        | slack         | Slack bot Web API token.                                                                |
| `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`        | slack         | Slack app-level Socket Mode token.                                                      |
| `SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN` | optional      | Verify the installed slash command through the Slack app manifest API.                  |
| `SLACK_API_URL`          | optional      | Override the Slack API URL for local testing. https:, or http: only on a loopback host. |
